sources.title: Anisotropic complex electrical conductivity of black shale and mudstone from the Moffat Shale Group (Ireland)
sources.reading_scope: Online relevant geological setting, electrical definitions, Materials and methods, Tables1/2, SIP measurements and mudstone discussion; not whole-paper reproduction
sources.sample_state: Intact oriented ordinary mudstone plugs vacuum-saturated48h with degassed NaCl solution, equilibrated at least24h; black shale and crushed samples excluded from default conductivity range
sources.adopted_part: DC conductivity order of magnitude and anisotropy warning only;3mS/m is our choice within these analogues
sources.not_adopted: The SIP relaxation times are not MHz dielectric Debye poles; no20-170MHz permittivity was inferred; NaCl saturation is not a site state

sources.title: Dielectric relaxation behavior of Callovo-Oxfordian clay rock: A hydraulic-mechanical-electromagnetic coupling approach
sources.reading_scope: Abstract and relevant sections3/4: specimen conditioning, coaxial inversion, Eq33, Fig4, Table4 and relaxation interpretation; PDF printed4733-4738 inspected in relevant portions, Eq33/Table4 visually checked; not whole-paper reproduction
sources.sample: French Bure Callovo-Oxfordian clay rock, varied saturation0.16 to almost1; intact and disturbed samples; not site red mudstone
sources.model: Generalized fractional relaxation: delta/((j*omega*tau)^a+(j*omega*tau)^b), plus apparent DC term
sources.adopted_part: Supports explicitly representing clay-rock dispersion/loss and using a nanosecond-scale research pole;8ns is our simplification
sources.not_adopted: No GDR spectrum reconstruction or single-Debye fit claimed. Source amplitudes/exponents and apparent DC term are not copied into gprMax Debye. Centre12/span3 are not source measurements. Table4 epsilon_S is the free-water-term static quantity, not20MHz effective permittivity.
